units.title: Keep full-check-run wording out of acceptance, and let the check gate settle test passing
units.task:
Stop the factory from writing, and from getting stuck on, acceptance that obliges the whole project check suite to pass or run (e.g. "all `dagger checks` pass", "all checks pass", "full check run is green"), and make reviewers take the service-owned check gate's passing result as the evidence that required tests ran.

1. Instructions. Update the architect's spec-and-plan drafting prompt, its amendment-drafting prompt and its workgroup delta prompt. They should say that acceptance states observable behaviours and may name tests a unit adds as evidence, never requires a whole-suite pass or run, and need not list existing tests to keep passing, because the factory's service-owned check gate (with smart-check selection) runs and selects checks itself and catches regressions. Update the architect/committee role policy so it treats whole-suite acceptance, or acceptance that asks a reviewer to show which tests ran, as an engineering defect to correct. Update the unit reviewer and final reviewer instructions so test passing is decided by the service-owned check gate: when the gate passed, every acceptance item or criterion requiring tests to pass (whole-suite, scoped or named) is satisfied as to passing, and a reviewer never raises a finding because only a smart-check selection ran, because it cannot see that a named test was selected, or because it cannot run tests. Reviewers still judge from the work whether tests the unit was asked to add exist and exercise the behaviour.

2. Guard. Add a detector that recognises spec criteria and unit acceptance items that oblige the work to make the whole check suite pass or run. It must distinguish obligations from mentions: text that describes, quotes, tests or prohibits whole-suite wording, and universals scoped to a named package or test set, are not obligations. Apply it at every admission path for new or revised plans: a new spec-and-plan draft (draft_write's verdict and the recorded draft), an amendment revision, and a workgroup delta delivered through deliver_delta. A match makes the submission invalid, with a problem that names the criterion (spec#<n>) or unit acceptance item and tells the architect to state the observable behaviour or the tests the unit adds instead. For amendments and workgroup deltas, check only criteria and acceptance items the revision adds or changes, never unchanged carried-over text, whether that text sits in a changed slice or an untouched one. Keep stored records loadable: trace migration and loading of already-recorded specs, plans, amendments and workgroup slices must not gain this rule.
acceptance: The architect's draft prompt, amendment prompt and workgroup delta prompt each tell the architect to state observable behaviours in acceptance (optionally naming tests the unit adds), never a whole-suite check pass or run and no list of existing tests to keep passing, and say that the factory runs and selects checks itself. Tests assert this guidance is present.
The architect/committee factory policy text carries the rule that whole-suite acceptance, or acceptance asking a reviewer to show which tests ran, is a defect to correct. Tests assert its presence.

The unit reviewer and final reviewer instructions say that a passing service-owned check gate is the evidence that required tests (whole-suite, scoped or named) ran and passed, and that a smart-check selection, an unseen named test, or the reviewer's inability to run tests is never a finding by itself. Tests assert this for each reviewer role.

Through the real draft_write tool path, a new draft whose spec criterion or unit acceptance item directly obliges the whole check suite to pass gets an invalid verdict, with a problem naming that criterion or unit item. When the turn completes, the recorded draft is invalid with the same problem.

Through the same draft_write path, a draft whose criteria and acceptance describe, quote, test or prohibit whole-suite wording (for example "acceptance never requires all checks to pass", "the validator rejects acceptance saying 'all checks pass'", "table tests flag 'full check run is green'") or use a scoped universal such as "all internal/plan tests pass" gets a valid verdict. A test submits this feature's own spec and plan text and finds no guard problem.

Through the amendment drafting path, a revision that adds or changes a whole-suite obligation is invalid. A revision that leaves an already-present such item unchanged and changes something else is not rejected for that item.

Through the real deliver_delta tool path for a workgroup delta, a proposed slice that adds or changes a whole-suite obligation is rejected with a problem naming it. Unchanged legacy whole-suite wording in a slice the delta changes, and in a slice it leaves untouched, does not cause a rejection.

Detector unit tests cover direct obligations (e.g. "all `dagger checks` pass", "dagger check passes", "full check run is green") as flagged, and specific tests, scoped universals, quoted examples and negated or prohibiting statements as not flagged.
A stored spec and plan, and a stored workgroup slice, that already contain whole-suite wording still pass trace migration (plan.DraftCheck) and load with no new problem.
boundaries: Smart check selection (internal/checkselect, smart_checks.go), candidate checks (unit_checks.go) and final checks (final_checks.go) stay as they are. This unit changes only wording, the validation of new or revised plans, and how reviewers read test-related acceptance.
Reviewers gain no way to run checks or choose a selection; they read the check gate's result as the service already provides it.
trace.Migrate's draft check (plan.DraftCheck) and every other read of stored records keep their current acceptance rules.
Workgroup change application, impact classification (internal/amendment) and delivery gates are unchanged; only what deliver_delta admits gains the guard for added or changed text.
guidance: The draft prompt is architectPrompt in internal/service/architect.go. The amendment prompt is in amendmentDrafter.enqueue in internal/service/amendment_draft.go. The workgroup delta turn is queued by queueChangeTurn in internal/service/workgroup_change_turns.go, and its changeTool validates proposed slices through drafter.validate. Role policy is factoryInstructions in internal/service/factory_policy.go (architectRole/committeeRole and reviewerRole). The final reviewer prompt is in internal/service/final_review.go. The unit review prompt may also carry its own wording about checks or tests; align it with the same rule.

The draft prompt's own instruction text currently tells the architect that acceptance includes 'the tests it adds or must keep passing'. Replace that phrase so it no longer asks for existing tests to keep passing.

plan.DraftProblems / plan.Validate also back plan.DraftCheck, which trace.Migrate applies to stored records. Adding the rule straight into Validate, or unconditionally into the shared drafter.validate, would break migration of historical plans or reject unchanged legacy slice text in unrelated deltas. Consider a separate exported check (e.g. in internal/plan) that takes the prior sealed text when there is one, applied from drafter.judge/record, amendmentDrafter.revision and the deliver_delta changeTool, with problem kinds consistent with existing Problem values.

For amendments, affectedRevision already computes changed criteria and touched units. For workgroup deltas, compare each proposed slice's criteria and acceptance items against that member's sealed slice so only new or changed text is checked.

Keep the detector narrow and obligation-shaped: an unscoped whole-suite subject (all/every/full/entire/complete checks, `dagger check` with no selection, the full test suite) used as a requirement on the work. Treat quoted text, negation (never/not/no), and statements about what a validator, detector or reviewer does as mentions. A scoped universal naming a package or test set is not whole-suite. Prefer missing an edge case over rejecting legitimate acceptance. The guard does not reject named-test or 'keep passing' wording; the reviewer rule settles those.
docs/design.md or docs/smart-checks.md may describe acceptance or check evidence. Update them if they say something contrary.
